display.title: Just for Hashem: A Chof Cheshvan Class and the Story of Reb Shmuel Brin
display.summary_short: On the Rebbe Rashab's birthday, a teacher tells a class about children who did mitzvos only for Hashem, then begins the story of Reb Shmuel Brin and the Rebbe Maharash.
display.summary_long: Recorded live in a boys' classroom on Chof Cheshvan, the birthday of the Rebbe Rashab. The teacher recalls collecting for pidyon shvuyim while Sholom Mordechai Rubashkin was in prison: one boy gave thirty dollars of his own money, and another said many chapters of Tehillim and refused a prize because he did it for Hashem. This reminds him of a Jew in Tzfas who would not reveal the special deed of his bar mitzvah even to Eliyahu HaNavi, because it was only for Hashem; that soul returned as the Baal Shem Tov. He adds the Rebbe Rashab's childhood wish to see Hashem like Avraham Avinu, and a mashal: asking for a lollipop to learn Torah is like refusing a million dollars unless a penny comes with it. Then comes story time: Reb Shmuel Brin, a Chassid of the Rebbe Maharash, is falsely accused when a worker steals from his vodka factory's government-metered tank, and he goes to the Rebbe for help. What the Rebbe advised is saved for next story time.
display.lesson: Do mitzvos and learn Torah for Hashem, not for prizes; Torah itself is the greatest reward.
